explanation: Each 30-day month held three ten-day weeks, called décades, plus five or six extra days at the end of the year. Napoleon scrapped it from 1 January 1806.

claims.text: The French Republican calendar divided each month into three ten-day weeks called décades.
The Republican week did not have five, seven or eight days.
The Republican calendar had twelve months of 30 days, plus five or six extra days at the end of the year.
Napoleon abolished the Republican calendar with effect from 1 January 1806.
